stubs.how: An ESM loader hook (.ui-capture/stub/loader.mjs) resolves the app's `node-fetch` import to .ui-capture/stub/fetch-stub.mjs. The stub looks the feed URL up in .ui-capture/fixtures/manifest.json and returns a real node-fetch Response with the fixture body and the content-type the real site sends (application/rss+xml, application/atom+xml, text/xml, application/json, application/feed+json, text/html). Unknown or dead URLs throw a real node-fetch FetchError (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). App source is unchanged.

app.notes: Bubo Reader is a static-site generator: `npm run build` (tsc) and then `node dist/index.js` fetch every feed in config/feeds.json and render config/template.html into public/index.html. Reproduce with `.ui-capture/build.sh`. It uses Node 18.12.1 from mise.toml (matching .nvmrc), runs npm ci and tsc, and then runs .ui-capture/seed/generate.mjs. The generator writes the feed fixtures plus a feeds.json in the app's own config format into a staging copy (.ui-capture/stage), so the repo's config/ and public/ stay untouched. It then runs the real compiled dist/index.js there with the fetch stub and copies stage/public (index.html and style.css) to .ui-capture/out. Data: 33 working feeds with 306 items, in 5 groups. Developer News has 8 feeds (Mozilla Hacks, web.dev, V8, A List Apart, CSS-Tricks, DEV, Changelog, WebKit). Blogs has 9 working feeds (George Mandis, Joy of Computing, Julia Evans, Simon Willison, Daring Fireball as a JSON Feed, a personal JSON-Feed blog with some title-less micro posts that fall back to showing their URL, rachelbythebay, Tim Bray, and a blog that went quiet about 7 months ago). Design has 4 working feeds (Smashing, NN/g, Ahmad Shadeed, Piccalilli). Reading & Misc has 4 (xkcd, Public Domain Review, Atlas Obscura, The Marginalian). My GitHub Projects has 6 (activity, release and commit Atom feeds). The feed URLs are the real ones, including all the originals from the repo's config. The repo's own feeds are kept; item titles and links are realistic but generated. Item dates are counted back from build time with a cadence per feed, so some feeds posted today and others are months or years stale. Two broken feeds make the template's Errors section show up: a lapsed domain (ENOTFOUND) and a blog page URL that returns HTML, which the XML parser rejects. Within each group, feeds appear in the order they finished fetching, as in real Bubo, and stub latencies are fixed per feed. UI: a single page with an h1, a heading per group, and one collapsible <details> per feed (feed title and feed URL, expanding to a dated list of item links). Below that are the Errors list and a footer with the 'Last updated' build timestamp and the Bubo version.
